Subject: Hosted API: Renewal cadence & capacity velocity upgrade proposal

Hi Elena —

Congrats on a strong Q2 launch — usage has been trending exactly where we anticipated. Per our renewal window next month, I wanted to propose an accelerated commit and a small rebanding of BrightCart's hosted API tiers to give you headroom for the upcoming holiday spike. High level:

- Current committed tokens/month: 1.2B
- Proposed committed tokens/month: 2.0B (effective on renewal date)
- New rate tiers: 0–1B @ $0.0009/token, 1B–3B @ $0.00075/token (effective blended pricing applied)
- Soft burst buffer: an additional 20% monthly burst credit with overage protection for the first 90 days

Goals: keep unit costs down through the seasonal window while avoiding throttling risk. If that sounds reasonable I'll put together a short mutual action plan (timeline, kickoff, billing cadence) and attach a draft SOF for budget/security review.

Attachments: usage_snapshot_Q2.csv (summary), draft SOF placeholder.

Proposed next steps: 30-min sync this week to confirm PO cadence and legal contact.

Thanks,
Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple quick Qs from our side before we take the draft to procurement:

1) Can you clarify how the soft burst buffer works in practice? We want guaranteed behavior around throttling during mid-month spikes.
2) Will the blended tiering be applied retroactively on the renewal invoice or forward from the renewal date?
3) We're sensitive to latency on large payloads — any plan-level latency SLOs tied to the upgraded commit?

We like the 2.0B proposed commit but procurement may ask for phased ramping (e.g., 1.5B first month, then 2.0B). I copied Carlos (ops) who will own implementation.

Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow morning ET?

Best,

Elena — quick technical notes to help procurement/ops evaluate: see inline.

1) Soft burst buffer: this is an automated monthly credit that allows temporary usage above committed tokens. For BrightCart we can configure a 20% buffer for 90 days with automatic graceful throttling thereafter. During buffer utilization we prioritize requests on your committed pool; if buffer is exhausted we route to a lower-cost compatible variant (e.g., quantized model family) rather than hard drop. We also provide request-level headers for burst diagnostics so you can observe token-by-token usage.

2) Billing: blended tiering in the proposal applies from the renewal effective date forward. We can, as a one-time courtesy, apply a retroactive credit for the first invoice if you hit >85% of the new commit in the prior billing term — we can document that in the SOF.

3) Latency: with the dedicated commit uplift we can guarantee p95 inference latency <= 220ms for your production chat routes under normal load. For very large payloads (>1.2k tokens) we recommend the heavier quantization profile be used for background batch jobs; interactive traffic will stay on the low-latency path.

Operational suggestion: stage the commit over two billing cycles — 1.5B for month 1, 1.75B for month 2, then 2.0B on month 3. This reduces procurement sticker shock and gives ops time to validate cache warming.

Let me know if you'd like me to add these options to the SOF.

-Karthik
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
